request.input:
Type the user question about the data-processing agreement below as exactly one closed claim type, or UNKNOWN. Call emit_claim exactly once. Type by what the question ASKS, not by what the answer might be. Today is 2026-11-20; resolve relative dates against it.

Clause inventory (ref + heading):
1 Parties
2 Definitions
3 Scope of processing
4 Purpose limitation
5 Data categories
6 Security safeguards
7 Processor engagement
8 Sub-processors
9.1 Cross-border transfers, general
9.2 Cross-border transfer for fraud screening
10 Breach intimation
11 Retention and erasure

User question: Summarise the entire agreement in one paragraph.

Closed types:
CT1 numeric_bound: the question compares a stated number (with unit) against a required bound. params: {"subject", "value" (number), "unit"}.
CT2 required_element: the question asks whether the agreement requires a specific element or duty. params: {"element"}.
CT3 in_force_on: the question asks whether a duty applies on a date. params: {"date" (YYYY-MM-DD), "subject"}; copy the date from the question, never invent one.
CT4 role_applies: the question asks whether a party holds a role under the agreement. params: {"party", "role"}.
UNKNOWN: opinion, summary, or anything no closed type can test. params: {} and a one-sentence explanation of why no type fits.

tools.name: emit_claim
tools.description: Type one user question about the agreement as CT1 numeric_bound, CT2 required_element, CT3 in_force_on, CT4 role_applies, or UNKNOWN with an explanation when no type fits.
